title: Berlin Wall Map: Quick Summary
items: **The Wall did not split Berlin down the middle.** It ran 155 kilometres around West Berlin, which was an island inside East Germany, so the line on the map is a loop and not a straight cut.
**Most of the famous historic centre was in the East:** Alexanderplatz and the World Clock, the TV Tower, Museum Island, the Berliner Dom and Unter den Linden.
**The Brandenburg Gate stood on East Berlin territory but sat inside the death strip,** with the Wall running in front of it on the western side from 1961 to 1989.
**Tap any point on the map** and it returns East Berlin, West Berlin, or on the Wall itself, plus the distance to the former fortification line.
**Anything within 25 metres of the line gets the on the Wall answer,** because at that distance the boundary and the real fortification overlap.
**The Wall geometry comes from the Berlin Open Data Portal,** the city's own surveying records, so it is accurate to within a few metres.
**The path is still readable on the ground.** A 1.3 kilometre double row of cobblestones marks the outer Wall line through the central city.
